content.title: Escalating Prop Failure | Brief Recovery and Runaway Payoff
content.summary: A courier repeatedly fixes a parcel-cart roof before it rolls away. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One character, prop and location remain fixed. + Every new attempt follows a visible failure. + A brief success precedes the stronger reversal. + Escalation changes prop behavior without resetting history. + The final departure pays off the repeated failures.
quick_start.recommended_input: Place one clearly adult animated courier in an orange rain coat at one flooded depot gate with a teal parcel cart. One hand reset briefly opens the roof correctly and she resumes pushing for two steps. The cart rolls out of frame with the courier running behind it, leaving the original gate and one spinning wheel in view.
required_anchors: One character, prop and location remain fixed.
Every new attempt follows a visible failure.
Escalation changes prop behavior without resetting history.
The final departure pays off the repeated failures.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: A courier repeatedly fixes a parcel-cart roof before it rolls away. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.

invariants.rule: One character, prop and location remain fixed.
invariants.purpose: Establishes the baseline identity, object or geography that every later state must preserve.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact baseline rule, later changes cannot be attributed to the same subject, object or place, so the sequence loses its reference state. Removed rule: "One character, prop and location remain fixed."

invariants.rule: Every new attempt follows a visible failure.
invariants.purpose: Makes the visible trigger precede and explain the first mechanism response.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact trigger rule, the response appears spontaneously and the central cause-and-effect claim is no longer demonstrated. Removed rule: "Every new attempt follows a visible failure."

invariants.rule: A brief success precedes the stronger reversal.
invariants.purpose: Keeps the middle progression registered instead of allowing an unexplained reset.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact progression rule, the middle can jump to a replacement state and the accumulated result is no longer traceable. Removed rule: "A brief success precedes the stronger reversal."

invariants.rule: Escalation changes prop behavior without resetting history.
invariants.purpose: Reconnects the changed or partial state to the established subject and spatial anchor.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact reconnection rule, detail or transformed shots can belong to a different subject or geography and continuity cannot be verified. Removed rule: "Escalation changes prop behavior without resetting history."

invariants.rule: The final departure pays off the repeated failures.
invariants.purpose: Turns the terminal hold into observable proof that the mechanism completed.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact terminal-proof rule, the sequence stops on motion alone and never confirms the promised outcome or preserved aftermath. Removed rule: "The final departure pays off the repeated failures."

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: all source faces, bodies, wardrobe, identities and creator-specific character designs
the source location, set dressing, props, products and exact environmental geometry
all source words, logos, watermarks, typefaces and brand identifiers
the source choreography, exact camera path, shot durations and transition timing
the source palette, signature effects, prompt wording, creator handle and narrative particulars
